coffee: Colombia Aponte Village Honey (2026 whole bean)
title: Onyx Colombia Aponte Village Honey 2026 review: red-honey fruit with two brew starts
description: Research-led US review of Onyx's 2026 Colombia Aponte Village Honey: Inga community lot, red-honey process, roaster notes, filter and espresso recipes, and dated buying limits.
imageAlt: Onyx Coffee Lab official Colombia Aponte Village Honey product image
imageCredit: Onyx Coffee Lab official 2026 product image, inspected November 12, 2026, for package identification. It is not Coffeedant photography or tasting.
price: Check the current US whole-bean checkout total
verdict: The 2026 Aponte Village Honey is a good small-bag trial for a buyer who wants a fruit-forward Colombian coffee with a documented red-honey process and separate filter and espresso starts. Onyx describes an Inga community field blend from Nariño and gives an Origami/Kalita 25:400 brew plus a 20:48 espresso target. Honeycrisp apple, cherry, vanilla and papaya are roaster notes; Coffeedant has not tasted the bag. Fellow's 2026 Advent guide independently supplies a smaller Stagg X start. The current page has contradictory caffeine metadata, so no caffeine claim is made. Check the exact 2026 whole-bean listing and delivered pack before ordering bulk.
bestFor: A fruit-led Colombian field blend with documented red-honey processing
Filter users who can try the published Origami/Kalita start
Espresso users willing to dial a separately stated 20:48 shot
skipIf: You prefer a chocolate-only or dark roast brief
You need a fixed named cultivar or identical lot across seasons
You want verified caffeine or sensory measurements from Coffeedant
authorNote: I checked Onyx's 2026 record, Fellow's current Advent brew guidance and dated owner observations. Coffeedant has not bought, brewed or tasted this coffee.

sections.title: A current Inga community lot, not a single cultivar
paragraphs: Onyx's 2026 page describes a community lot assembled from producers around Aponte in Nariño, Colombia, at about 2,100 metres. Its story says Onyx cupped 38 individual producer lots and chose 18 for this seasonal build. The named variety is a field blend rather than one cultivar, and the process is red honey. These are roaster-supplied sourcing details for the checked release, not a promise that next year's Aponte coffee will use the same farms or proportions. [1]

Onyx describes partial drying before depulping and then drying with mucilage retained. That distinguishes this coffee from a washed Colombia on the shelf and from its separately sold instant Aponte product. The site's own caffeine module displays '0 mg/12 oz' despite the page describing ordinary caffeinated coffee, so this review does not repeat or interpret that field as a decaf claim. Ask the roaster about a specific caffeine requirement. [1] [7]

sections.title: Red fruit is the roaster's design brief
paragraphs: Onyx lists Honeycrisp apple, cherry, vanilla and papaya for the current 2026 product. Its story also describes structured sweetness and red-fruit character, with the red-honey processing offered as context. These are Onyx's sensory descriptions, not Coffeedant tasting or a certainty about any one bag. A recorded light roast and ground Agtron #128 describe a roast sample rather than a universal flavor score. [1]

Fellow's 2026 Advent guide names Aponte Village Honey with a similar honeycrisp/cherry/vanilla direction and an additional butterscotch word. A May 2026 owner reported a fresh, enjoyable bag; an older 2025 Advent owner described clarity and silky body in their own V60. Those are different samples and self-selected experiences. They help frame a trial but cannot establish the exact taste of a November 2026 whole-bean pack. [2] [4] [5]

sections.title: The roaster gives separate filter and shot targets
paragraphs: Onyx publishes an Origami or Kalita Wave 185 start of 25 g coffee to 400 g water at 205°F, a 1:16 ratio, with staged pours and a stated 3:30 drain target. Fellow's 2026 Advent Stagg X guidance uses 18 g to 280 g at 204°F, about 1:15.6, with a longer target on its own equipment. These are different flat-bottom recipes and samples, not contradictory measured Coffeedant outcomes. Start with the one that matches your brewer, then adjust to your actual cup. [1] [2]

For espresso, Onyx lists 20 g in to 48 g out with a pressure-profile outline. Use that only if the basket accommodates 20 g; water, roast date, grinder and machine alter the needed setting. A public owner shot record from an earlier 2026 roast used 17 g to 51.2 g under their own setup and recorded a different subjective flavor direction. That is useful evidence that espresso recipes vary, not a replacement for Onyx's start or a Coffeedant shot measurement. [1] [3]

sections.title: Verify the actual roast and release
paragraphs: Onyx says its direct online coffee is roasted to order on weekdays and gives guidance for rolling an opened 10 oz inner bag into its box. That direct practice does not establish the roast date of a third-party bag. Inspect the box and date you receive, store whole beans tightly sealed away from heat and moisture, and grind near brewing. Onyx advises an airtight container for larger opened packs. [6]

The product page shows a live inventory figure and dynamic cart but does not expose a dependable selected size-and-price pair in the accessible record. Do not infer that a specific size remains in stock merely because it appears in a cached search result. Start with a small whole-bean format and check the current 2026 suffix, shipping and tax at checkout before committing to a larger seasonal pack. [1]

sections.title: The first bag tests whether fruit earns the premium
paragraphs: This coffee has more decision-useful sourcing and recipe detail than an anonymous 'Colombian honey' listing: producer community, field-blend identity, process, roast description and two brew starts. It has no Coffeedant price-per-cup or tasting score. Compare the selected US pack and delivered total in the live cart, then decide whether the actual fruit-led result warrants another bag while this seasonal lot remains available. [1] [2]

A process label is not enough by itself. If your usual cup is a large chocolate-heavy milk drink, a darker Onyx Monarch may fit better; if you want a lighter year-round blend with broader origin rotation, Onyx Geometry is a different route. Neither is a sensory clone. Aponte's value is most credible when the buyer actually makes the filter or espresso recipe and appreciates the fruit direction, not when buying bulk for the name alone. [1] [8] [9]

sections.title: Compare the exact coffee and release year
paragraphs: Onyx Geometry is a year-round blend with a more general daily-drink purpose, while Monarch is a darker espresso and milk choice. Aponte is a single-country, community-built seasonal lot with red-honey processing and a more fruit-forward brief. Those contrasts come from current roaster records and Coffeedant's existing reviews, not a side-by-side tasting here. [1] [8] [9]

The Onyx Aponte -25 page and earlier Advent calendars are historical references, not substitutes for the -26 whole-bean listing. Distinguish the pack from instant Aponte and from other roasters' Aponte coffees before comparing prices or owner experiences. A shared producing community does not imply the same roaster, lot or cup. [1] [7]

faqs.question: Is this the 2026 whole-bean Aponte release?
faqs.answer: Yes. This review follows Onyx's current /colombia-aponte-village-honey-26 listing, not its older -25 or instant product.

faqs.question: What does red honey mean here?
faqs.answer: Onyx describes partial drying before depulping and further drying with fruit mucilage remaining. The process label does not predict your exact cup.

faqs.question: What does it taste like?
faqs.answer: Onyx lists Honeycrisp apple, cherry, vanilla and papaya. Coffeedant has not tasted this release.

faqs.question: What filter recipe does Onyx publish?
faqs.answer: Its Origami/Kalita start is 25 g coffee to 400 g water at 205°F, with staged pours and a 3:30 drain target.

faqs.question: Can it be brewed as espresso?
faqs.answer: Onyx lists a 20 g dose to 48 g beverage starting target. Dial in your own basket, grinder and machine.

faqs.question: Is the 0 mg caffeine figure reliable?
faqs.answer: The page's 0 mg module conflicts with the ordinary caffeinated coffee identity, so this review makes no caffeine amount or decaf claim. Ask Onyx for a specific need.
